subject: RHadoop not working: Java heap space error

messages.author: b18df2f5370502b2
messages.subject: RHadoop not working: Java heap space error
parts:
Hello!

I am trying to get RHadoop working on a Hadoop cluster.

This is a test cluster for development / proof of concept.
It has 5 nodes, virtualized in VMware.
The OS on all nodes is centos 6.4

To install R on Hadoop, I followed these instructions:
https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki

The following example analysis is constantly failing with a Java heap size error:

groups = rbinom(100, n = 500, prob = 0.5)
tapply(groups, groups, length)
require('rmr2')
groups = rbinom(100, n = 500, prob = 0.5)
groups = to.dfs(groups)
result = mapreduce(
    input = groups,
    map = function(k,v) keyval(v, 1),
    reduce = function(k,vv) keyval(k, length(vv)))
print(result())
print(from.dfs(result, to.data.frame=T))


The code above is from this repo:
https://github.com/hortonworks/HDP-Public-Utilities/tree/master/Installation/r#rhadoop-validation

Any help to get this solved would be very much appreciated!

Best,

Manuel

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#1642] RHadoop not working: Java heap space error
parts:
Please consult the debugging guide first.


Antonio
On Mon, Sep 1, 2014 at 10:11 AM, Manuel <manue...@googlemail.com> wrote:

Hello!

I am trying to get RHadoop working on a Hadoop cluster.

This is a test cluster for development / proof of concept.
It has 5 nodes, virtualized in VMware.
The OS on all nodes is centos 6.4

To install R on Hadoop, I followed these instructions:
https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki

The following example analysis is constantly failing with a Java heap size error:

groups = rbinom(100, n = 500, prob = 0.5)
tapply(groups, groups, length)
require('rmr2')
groups = rbinom(100, n = 500, prob = 0.5)
groups = to.dfs(groups)
result = mapreduce(
    input = groups,
    map = function(k,v) keyval(v, 1),
    reduce = function(k,vv) keyval(k, length(vv)))
print(result())
print(from.dfs(result, to.data.frame=T))


The code above is from this repo:
https://github.com/hortonworks/HDP-Public-Utilities/tree/master/Installation/r#rhadoop-validation

Any help to get this solved would be very much appreciated!

Best,

Manuel

parts:
Many thanks for the quick feedback and the link!

Meanwhile I would like to add some further information on software versions used, just in case:
* plyrmr_0.4.0.tar.gz
* rhdfs_1.0.8.tar.gz
* rmr2_3.2.0.tar.gz
* epel-release-6-8.noarch.rpm
* rstudio-server-0.98.1028-x86_64.rpm
* R 3.1.0 (2014-04-10)

Best,

Manuel
On Monday, September 1, 2014 7:11:38 PM UTC+2, Manuel wrote:

Hello!

I am trying to get RHadoop working on a Hadoop cluster.

This is a test cluster for development / proof of concept.
It has 5 nodes, virtualized in VMware.
The OS on all nodes is centos 6.4

To install R on Hadoop, I followed these instructions:
https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki

The following example analysis is constantly failing with a Java heap size error:

groups = rbinom(100, n = 500, prob = 0.5)
tapply(groups, groups, length)
require('rmr2')
groups = rbinom(100, n = 500, prob = 0.5)
groups = to.dfs(groups)
result = mapreduce(
    input = groups,
    map = function(k,v) keyval(v, 1),
    reduce = function(k,vv) keyval(k, length(vv)))
print(result())
print(from.dfs(result, to.data.frame=T))


The code above is from this repo:
https://github.com/hortonworks/HDP-Public-Utilities/tree/master/Installation/r#rhadoop-validation

Any help to get this solved would be very much appreciated!

Best,

Manuel

On Monday, September 1, 2014 7:11:38 PM UTC+2, Manuel wrote:
Hello!

I am trying to get RHadoop working on a Hadoop cluster.

This is a test cluster for development / proof of concept.
It has 5 nodes, virtualized in VMware.
The OS on all nodes is centos 6.4

To install R on Hadoop, I followed these instructions:
https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki

The following example analysis is constantly failing with a Java heap size error:

groups = rbinom(100, n = 500, prob = 0.5)
tapply(groups, groups, length)
require('rmr2')
groups = rbinom(100, n = 500, prob = 0.5)
groups = to.dfs(groups)
result = mapreduce(
    input = groups,
    map = function(k,v) keyval(v, 1),
    reduce = function(k,vv) keyval(k, length(vv)))
print(result())
print(from.dfs(result, to.data.frame=T))


The code above is from this repo:
https://github.com/hortonworks/HDP-Public-Utilities/tree/master/Installation/r#rhadoop-validation

Any help to get this solved would be very much appreciated!

Best,

Manuel

parts:
I installed rmr2_3.2.1 (version from 2014-09-02) and tried the tutorial:
https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/rmr2/blob/master/docs/tutorial.md

The first example (with only the map phase) works.
The second example (with map and reduce) still crashes.

I tried the tutorial from above as well with the previous version, rmr2_3.2.0.
Map phase only works, reduce phase crashes with Java heap space error.

Please find below the logs for the runs with rmr2_3.2.1

Best,

Manuel

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#1652] Re: RHadoop not working: Java heap space error
parts:
For the record, this is not the logs, nor the type of logs that the debugging guide recommends to look for initially. In this case though I think you are onto something with this log. Until recently, I think the last version, we let Hadoop run at configuration defaults with rmr jobs. That doesn't work very well with YARN because containers are monitored for memory use and java is allocated most of the space and R is left with nothing. So we set up rmr2 to modify the configuration for each job as follows

$hadoop
$hadoop$D
[1] "mapreduce.map.java.opts=-Xmx400M"

$hadoop$D
[1] "mapreduce.reduce.java.opts=-Xmx400M"

$hadoop$D
[1] "mapreduce.map.memory.mb=4096"

$hadoop$D
[1] "mapreduce.reduce.memory.mb=4096"


The values  have been generated asking around and trying a few jobs. They may be in need of refinement or maybe it's impossible to set them in a way that covers most needs. In your specific case it appears that mapreduce.reduce.java.opts is set too low. I am not sure why 400M shouldn't be enough though, as you are running one of the standard examples. Anyway, let's push that higher and see if we get through the reduce phase, at least we will have learnt something. To do that, get the current confguration:

bp  = rmr.options("backend.parameters")

#change

bp$hadoop[2] = "mapreduce.reduce.java.opts=-Xmx800M"

#check
bp

#set

rmr.options(backend.parameters = bp)

#check

rmr.options("backend.parameters")

And rerun. If it goes through, you have a workaround and I have a clue to work from, at least. In alternative or combination, you could try to increase mapreduce.reduce.memory.mb following similar steps. Thanks


Antonio
On Thu, Sep 4, 2014 at 6:58 AM, Manuel <manue...@googlemail.com> wrote:

I installed rmr2_3.2.1 (version from 2014-09-02) and tried the tutorial:
https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/rmr2/blob/master/docs/tutorial.md

The first example (with only the map phase) works.
The second example (with map and reduce) still crashes.

I tried the tutorial from above as well with the previous version, rmr2_3.2.0.
Map phase only works, reduce phase crashes with Java heap space error.

Please find below the logs for the runs with rmr2_3.2.1

Best,

Manuel
